FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the dra ft finalized by the Rock MechaDlcs Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineer ing Div ision Council. Natural rock formal ions are in triaxially stressed state and the strength characteristic of rock under such a state IS important in calculating the hearing capacity of foundation of rock and is also useful in slope stability analysis. ThIS standard is based on the suggested method of International Society of Rock Mechanics. In reporting the rerults of a test or analyais marle 10 accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, IS to be rounded off,.t shall be done In accordance with IS 2: 19bU 'Rules for rounding off numerical values (,eulSed)' .

Indian Standard

METHOD FOR DETERMINATION OF STRENGTH OF ROCK MATERIALS IN TRIAXIAL COMPRESSION
I SCOPE
1.1 This standard covers the mothod for deterrnination of strength of cyhndncal rock specimens subjected to triaxial compression. This test provides Individual points on the failure (peak strength) envelope from several tests. From this the value of the internal friction angle '" and the apparent cohesion C may be obtained. 1.2 Thisstandard does not cover (a) the multiple failure state test, and (b) the continuous failure state test wherein the failure envelope is produced with a single test employing a stepwise or continuous procedure.
Df3. Surfaces of the piatens shall be ground and these shall not depart from plane surfaces by more than +0 005 mm. c) The top platen which shall incorporate a spherical seat. The centre of curvature of the spherical seat should coincide with the centre ot the top surface of the specimen. The spherical seat shall be lightly lubricated WIth mineral oil. The specimen, the platens and the spherical seat shall be accurately central with respect to one
another.

The membrane shall not penetrate significantly into the surface pores and it shall be sufficiently long to extend well on to the platens. When shghtly stretched, it shall be of the same diameter as the specimen. When strain gauged specimens are tested, a moulded silicon rubber membrane is satisfactory.

5.6 The axial load on the test specimen shan then be increased continuously and without shock to produce an approximately constant rate of load or deformation; such that failure will occur within 5 to 15 rmnutes of irutianon of loading If carrred to failure Alternatively the stress rate shall he withm the limits of 0'5 to 1'0 MPafs. The axial failure load shall be measured withm 1 percent accuracy.

7 REPORT
7.1 The report shall give a plot of axial strength versus confining pressure as discussed in 6.2 ( Fig. 3 ), along WIth the values of apparent coheSIOn c and angle of internal friction", citing the lange of confining pressures in which they are vahd,

5.9 The number of specimens to be tested, as well
as) the number of different confining pressure values should be determined from practical consideracrons. However, at least five speccmeus- per rock sample are preferred.

6 CALCULATIONS
6.1 The compressive strength of the specimen shall be calculated by dividmg the maximum axial load, applied to the specimen during the tes t, by the original cross sectional area of the specimen.

7.2 The report of test shall also include the following information:
a) Lithologic description of rock. b) Orientation of the axis of loading WIth respect to anisotropy, bedding planes, fohations, etc.
c) Source of sample, location, depth, onentation and date of sampling. d) Storage history and environment.

6.'2 The confining pressures and the correspond109 strength values for different specimen as worked out m 6.1, are plotted WIth the confining pressures as abscissa and strength as ordinates lseeFtg3).

6.3 A strength envelope IS obtained by fitting a mean curve to the above points. From practical considerations It may be advisable to fit a straight hne to only the most relevant pal t of the curve or to fit several straight lines to different parts of the curve. Each straight line IS characterised by calculatmg its gradient m ( tangent of the inchnation) its intercept b on the vertical (axial stress) axis (see Fig. 3). In each case the range 01 confinmg pressure in which the respective straight Ime IS valid shall be shown on the abscissa.
m

e) Moisture content of sample and room temperature at the time of the test. f) Duration of the test and stress rate. g) Date of testing and type of machine used. h) Number of specimens tested. j) Mode of failure of each specimen ( with sketch showing failure pattern ). k) Other physical properties such as specific gravity, absorption, permeability and porosity, citing the Indian Standard available for the determination of the above properties.
